properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): the handshake record's `negotiated` comes from reflow2's hand copy of rmcp's pub(crate) negotiation rule, copied at 3.1.2. By 3.4.0 rmcp echoed only a version that still has an `initialize` handshake, and the copy echoed any supported one. Its only test pinned the copy against itself. The wire stayed right, because rmcp re-runs its own rule on what the override returns, but the record could name a revision the client never received
properties.source: reflow2 branch deps/rmcp-3-5-and-lock-refresh (commit 90f83a0 + test revision); rmcp-3.4.0 and rmcp-3.5.0 src/service/server.rs; cargo test output 2026-10-02
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-02, dev_reflow2 hub session, while doing the approved rmcp 3.4.0 → 3.5.0 bump (fact:rmcp-3-5-0-moves-latest-to-2026-07-28-and-reflow2s-pin-will-fail-by-design-2026-10-01).

① OBSERVED, over the real binary, with the pre-fix rule restored and rmcp 3.5.0: the test reported `initialize(2026-07-28): the record says negotiated was "2026-07-28" but rmcp sent 2025-11-25`. The test is tests/an_initialize_is_recorded_as_rmcp_answered_it.rs::the_handshake_record_names_the_version_rmcp_sent on branch deps/rmcp-3-5-and-lock-refresh. The record was `<graph>.client.json`. EXPECTED: the record's `negotiated` equals the version on the wire. NOT AFFECTED: the wire answer itself, and every requested revision that has a handshake.

② PRECEDENT: the same class was root-caused 2026-09-26 in fact:root-cause-the-latent-tool-list-omits-the-cache-fields-the-2026-07-28-spec-requires-2026-09-26. reflow2 overrides an rmcp method, rmcp's rule is pub(crate) or inline in a macro, and each override reproduces it by hand. This is the second instance, in a different override (`initialize`, src/service.rs).

③/④ CANDIDATES AND WHAT SEPARATES THEM:
- (a) The copy drifted from rmcp. If true, rmcp's rule differs from the copy's in some release ≤ 3.4.0.
- (b) rmcp changed nothing, and the record is right while the wire is wrong. If true, rmcp's serve path would echo the requested version.
- (c) I measured the wrong thing. The record is written before rmcp's second negotiation, so maybe they are not comparable.
Reading rmcp 3.4.0 src/service/server.rs:480-505 shows `is_legacy_version(client_requested) && server_supported.contains(..)` and a fallback to the newest legacy version. The copy (src/handshake.rs, cited "rmcp 3.1.2's own doc comment") has neither. rmcp 3.4.0 and 3.5.0 serve_server (:652-663 / :658-668) re-run negotiation on the override's answer and set peer_info to the result. That supports (a), refutes (b), and makes (c) the defect itself: the record is taken from the copy, not from the wire.

⑤ MEASURED as above: the wire said 2025-11-25 and the record said 2026-07-28.

⑥ THE CLASS: a rule maintained by hand, with a test that compares the copy with itself (`negotiation_mirrors_rmcp` asserted only that the copy echoes supported versions). The comment claimed "a change in rmcp is LOUD", and nothing could make it loud. The same class as the latent tool list.

⑦ PINNED over the real binary, for every revision rmcp knows plus 2024-01-01 and 2027-01-01. It compares the record with the wire, so it fails on ANY future divergence, not only this one. OBSERVED FAILING against the pre-fix rule (above).

⑧ FIX: handshake::negotiate is rmcp 3.5.0's rule (src/service/server.rs:486), returning None as rmcp's refusal. The `initialize` override returns rmcp's own unsupported_protocol_version error on None. The copy's doc comment now says it drifted and which test keeps it honest.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: when exactly between 3.1.2 and 3.4.0 rmcp's rule changed (3.1.2's doc comment matched the copy, so somewhere in 3.2–3.4), and whether any real client ever asked for 2026-07-28 through `initialize` and so got a wrong record. The record is diagnostic only. No served answer read it.
